Formulation  
Current consultation focused on physical health (heart-failure exacerbation). No specific mental health condition elicited; minor situational anxiety related to breathlessness and employment. Predisposing factors: chronic cardiac illness; living alone. Precipitating factor: recent increase in dyspnea and ankle edema. Perpetuating factors: limited social support, work stress. Protective factors: engagement with GP, willingness to follow treatment, abstinent from alcohol, ex-smoker.  

Mental Health Care Plan Details  
(No principal mental health problem identified in transcript. Plan below addresses sub-clinical worry and supports adjustment to chronic illness.)  

Principal Problem: Health-related worry/adjustment to chronic cardiac illness  
- Patient Goal(s): Reduce health-related worry; maintain ability to work; understand condition and management  
- Clinical Goal(s): Monitor for emerging anxiety/depression; provide psychoeducation; support coping with chronic disease  
- Actions (Patient):  
  • Follow medication changes and monitoring as instructed  
  • Note triggers of worry; practice relaxation (e.g., slow breathing)  
  • Seek earlier review if anxiety increases or mood declines  
- Actions (Clinician/GP):  
  • Provide written information on heart failure and symptom management  
  • Screen for anxiety/depression at next review (e.g., GAD-7, PHQ-9)  
  • Offer referral to cardiac rehabilitation program with psychosocial support if available

- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased breathlessness, chest pain, palpitations, dizziness, rising anxiety  
- Coping Strategies: Slow-breathing techniques, pacing activities, contacting GP promptly if concerned
